title: unify-span-propagation-and-metrics-adapter
creator: Liam O'Rourke
description:
Scope: Consolidate trace context propagation and standardize our metrics adapter surface across the serving runtime and SDKs. This ticket addresses accumulated tech debt from divergent tracing hooks and ad-hoc metrics clients that increase overhead and cause inconsistent dashboards.

Goals:
- Migrate all runtime services to a single OpenTelemetry runtime client version (target: OTEL SDK v1.12) and a shared span context propagation implementation using W3C TraceContext and custom baggage mappings.
- Replace three internal metrics shim layers with a single metrics adapter that emits Prometheus-compatible metrics and enforces cardinality limits and stable label naming.
- Reduce end-to-end CPU and memory overhead from tracing/metrics by ~15% under p95 load (measured in our load tests).
- Provide a rollback plan and feature-flag rollout to avoid user-visible regressions.

Out of scope: full rework of logging format (separate ticket), APM vendor migration (we will keep existing exporters but centralize export configuration).

Acceptance criteria:
1) All runtime services compile and run with OTEL SDK v1.12 and the unified propagation module behind a feature flag.
2) Integration tests validate propagation across service boundaries for sampled and unsampled spans.
3) Representative loadtest shows <= 5% added tail latency and >= 15% reduction in tracing-related CPU/memory compared to current baseline.
4) Dashboards updated with new metric names and a migration notice; alerts adjusted to new cardinality.
5) Gradual rollout plan documented and tested; rollback steps verified in staging.
comments: 2026-02-01 - Liam O'Rourke: Created ticket after postmortem shows inconsistent spans during the 2026-01-29 incident. Initial investigation: three propagation helpers across runtime, public API SDK, and admin agent. Metrics tag explosion in `runtime.request` recorded in Grafana.

2026-02-07 - Maya Chen: Spiked a prototype adapter (branch: feat/otel-adapter-spike). Prototype uses OTEL v1.12, W3C propagation, and a simple label sanitizer. Early numbers: ~12% CPU improvement on tracer hotpath in microbenchmark. Uploaded benchmark results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8341#issuecomment-1999999

2026-02-14 - Design review: Agreed on label naming conventions and rejecting per-request dynamic labels except for a stable `route` label. Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/OTEL-Migration

2026-02-20 - Eng sync: Decided to use a phased rollout behind `observability.unified_adapter` feature flag. Phase 1: runtime internal services only; Phase 2: SDKs and public API clients. Also decided to keep exporters pluggable (Prometheus + OTLP) to avoid vendor lock-in.
2026-02-28 - QA: Integration tests added for trace propagation across GRPC->HTTP boundary. Found a bug where baggage was dropped for admin-agent spawned child processes; created followup ENG-15809.

2026-03-04 - Perf: Load test run 2026-03-03 shows 16% reduction in tracer CPU and 9% reduction in memory under steady-state with sampling set to 1%. p95 latency within SLO. Uploaded graphs: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/otel-migration?view=perf-2026-03-03
2026-03-10 - Security review request: Submitted high-level design for review (no secrets change). Security asked for a checklist on header sanitization; added to PR checklist.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Open PR created for adapter and propagation changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8420. Marked as target for runtime-1.20 staging deploy. Requesting two reviewers from infra and sdk teams.
